input: Track all household subscriptions in one spreadsheet

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Subscriptions can range from streaming and software to gym memberships, meal kits, and insurance — knowing which categories to include defines how many rows and columns the sheet needs.
If multiple household members share or own separate subscriptions, the sheet may need an 'owner' column or separate tabs per person, changing the structure.
Whether the user is starting from scratch or migrating from an existing list (notes app, bank statements, memory) determines the data-gathering step required before building.
The tool available (Google Sheets, Excel, Notion, Airtable) directly determines formulas, sharing options, and template format.
The primary use — cancellation decisions, budgeting, renewal reminders — changes which columns and calculations to prioritise (e.g. cost totals vs. renewal dates vs. a 'worth it' rating).
Knowing whether 'done well' means a simple static list or a live tracker with alerts and auto-totals determines the complexity of formulas and automation needed.
Whether the user wants a ready-made template to fill in or step-by-step guidance to build it themselves changes the format of the output entirely.

gold.taskTitle: Track all household subscriptions in one spreadsheet
gold.taskDescription: Build a single spreadsheet to log and monitor every recurring subscription the household pays for.

questions.title: Which subscription categories should be included?
questions.description: Determine the scope: streaming, software, fitness, food delivery, insurance, utilities, etc. — or everything without exception.

questions.title: How many people's subscriptions need to be tracked?
questions.description: Establish whether this covers one person, a couple, or a full family — and whether individual ownership needs to be recorded.

questions.title: Do you already have a list, or starting from scratch?
questions.description: Find out if the user needs to audit and gather subscriptions first or if they have data ready to enter.

questions.title: Which tool will you build this spreadsheet in?
questions.description: Identify the platform — Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, Notion, Airtable, or another — to tailor the template and formulas accordingly.

questions.title: What is the main goal: budgeting, reminders, or reviewing value?
questions.description: Clarify the primary purpose so the most important columns (cost totals, renewal dates, a value rating) are prioritised in the design.

questions.title: Do you want automatic totals and renewal alerts, or a simple list?
questions.description: Decide whether the sheet should include live calculations, conditional formatting, or calendar alerts, versus a straightforward static log.

questions.title: Do you want a ready-made template or to build it yourself?
questions.description: Determine whether to deliver a filled-in template to copy, or step-by-step instructions for the user to construct it on their own.
